chunks.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ الْوَلِيدِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ عَنِ الْمُفَضَّلِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ع قَالَ

translations.en: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from al-Mufaddal ibn Qays from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: كَمْ شِيعَتُنَا بِالْكُوفَةِ قَالَ قُلْتُ خَمْسُونَ أَلْفًا قَالَ فَمَا زَالَ يَقُولُ حَتَّى قَالَ أَ تَرْجُو أَنْ يَكُونُوا عِشْرِينَ ثُمَّ قَالَ ع- وَ اللَّهِ لَوَدِدْتُ أَنْ يَكُونَ بِالْكُوفَةِ خَمْسَةٌ وَ عِشْرُونَ رَجُلًا يَعْرِفُونَ أَمْرَنَا الَّذِي نَحْنُ عَلَيْهِ وَ لَا يَقُولُونَ عَلَيْنَا إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ

translations.en: He asked: How many are our Shia in Kufa? I said: Fifty thousand. He kept saying (implying 'is that all?' or 'do you hope for less?') until he said: Do you hope they were twenty? Then he said: By Allah, I wish that there were in Kufa twenty-five men who know our matter (belief/affair) which we are upon, and do not say about us except the truth.

en.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Sifat al-Shia* highlights the Imam’s preference for a core of twenty-five knowledgeable men who accurately represent their teachings, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *taqiyya* and precise doctrinal fidelity over mere numerical strength. Historically, Kufa was a pivotal center for Shia political and religious life, making this assessment of its elite followers particularly significant for understanding the development of Shia identity during the Imamate period. The Imam’s wish underscores that true Shi'ism is defined by deep understanding and truthful representation rather than crowd size.
en.seo_question: What did the Imam prefer regarding the number of his followers in Kufa?

key_terms.أَمْرَنَا: Our matter/affair (referring to beliefs and teachings)
